intro: Copenhagen rewards visitors with canals, design, and cozy hygge at every turn. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro runs 24/7; M1/M2 link the airport to the centre in about 14 min.
S-trains and buses cover the city; a 3-zone ticket costs about DKK30.
Taxis are metered and pricey; apps like Uber and Bolt operate in the city.
Driving in the centre is slow and parking is costly; park outside and take transit.
The city is flat and bike-friendly; rental bikes are everywhere.
Harbour buses and small ferries cross the canals cheaply.

nyhavn.name: Nyhavn
nyhavn.price_text: Free to walk · canal boat tours from about DKK 100
nyhavn.hours: Always open · restaurants and bars from late morning to late night
nyhavn.tip: Come before 09:00 for photos without crowds, then return at sunset for the coloured houses lit up.

tivoli.name: Tivoli Gardens
tivoli.price_text: Entry about DKK 140–160 · rides extra (multi-ride wristband about DKK 300)
tivoli.hours: Seasonal · usually mid-April to late September, plus Christmas season · check on the day
tivoli.tip: Buy the entry ticket and ride wristband online to skip the queue, and stay after dark for the lights.

little-mermaid.name: The Little Mermaid
little-mermaid.tip: The statue is small and busy. Combine it with a walk along the Langelinie promenade rather than making a special trip.

amalienborg.name: Amalienborg
amalienborg.price_text: Free to see the square · palace museum about DKK 100–120
amalienborg.hours: Square always open · changing of the guard daily around 11:30–12:00 · museum hours check on the day
amalienborg.tip: Stand in the middle of the square to see the guard march past, and check the flag to see if the Queen is home.

rosenborg.name: Rosenborg Castle
rosenborg.hours: Usually 10:00–16:00 · check on the day, closed some Mondays
rosenborg.tip: See the Crown Jewels in the basement, then relax in the King's Garden next door for free.

christiansborg.name: Christiansborg Palace
christiansborg.price_text: About DKK 150–170 for the main palace · tower free
christiansborg.tip: The palace tower is free and gives one of the best views in the city. Go up before the palace tour.

round-tower.name: The Round Tower
round-tower.hours: Usually 10:00–20:00 in summer · shorter in winter, check on the day
round-tower.tip: Walk the spiral ramp to the top for a 360° view of the old town. No lift, but the slope is easy.

canal-tour.name: Canal Tours Copenhagen
canal-tour.hours: Departures roughly 09:30–17:00, more often in summer · check on the day
canal-tour.tip: Boats leave from Nyhavn. Sit on the open back deck for the best views and photos.

carlsberg.name: Carlsberg Brewhouse
carlsberg.tip: The ticket includes beer samples. Go by train to Carlsberg station, it is a short walk from there.

opera-house.name: Copenhagen Opera House
opera-house.price_text: Tickets vary by performance · check the programme
opera-house.hours: Performance times vary · foyer open before shows
opera-house.tip: Even without a ticket, take the harbour bus or walk over for the building and waterfront view.

zoo.name: Copenhagen Zoo
zoo.hours: Usually 10:00–17:00, longer in summer · check on the day
zoo.tip: Big and hilly. Wear good shoes and plan at least half a day, especially with children.

bakken.name: Dyrehavsbakken
bakken.price_text: Free entry · rides paid per ride or wristband
bakken.hours: Seasonal, roughly April to August · check on the day
bakken.tip: The world's oldest amusement park. Combine it with a walk in the deer park next door.

christiania.name: Freetown Christiania
christiania.hours: Daytime is best · avoid Pusher Street area
christiania.tip: Photography is not allowed in parts of Christiania. Respect the signs and keep to the main paths.

parken.name: Parken Stadium
parken.price_text: Match tickets vary · tours when available
parken.hours: Only on match days or tours · check the fixture list
parken.tip: Check if FC Copenhagen or Denmark are playing at home. Book tickets early for big games.

royal-theatre.name: Royal Danish Theatre
royal-theatre.price_text: Tickets vary by performance · check the programme
royal-theatre.tip: The old stage on Kongens Nytorv is worth a look even without a ticket. Check for cheaper last-minute seats.

black-diamond.name: Royal Library of Copenhagen (Black Diamond)
black-diamond.price_text: Free to enter the building and exhibitions
black-diamond.hours: Usually 08:00–20:00 weekdays, shorter at weekends · check on the day
black-diamond.tip: Walk up to the top floor for the view over the harbour, then sit in the glass atrium cafe.

smorrebrod.name: Smørrebrød lunch
smorrebrod.price_text: About DKK 80–120 per piece · lunch with drinks about DKK 200–350
smorrebrod.hours: Lunchtime, roughly 11:30–15:00 · book ahead at classic places
smorrebrod.tip: Order two or three pieces, not one. Try pickled herring first, then roast beef with remoulade.

stortorget.name: Stortorget, Malmö
stortorget.price_text: Free · train from Copenhagen about SEK 100–150 each way
stortorget.tip: A day trip over the Øresund bridge. The train takes about 35 minutes from Copenhagen Central.

blue-planet.name: The Blue Planet (Den Bla Planet)
blue-planet.hours: Usually 10:00–17:00, longer in summer · check on the day
blue-planet.tip: It is near the airport, not the centre. Take the metro to Kastrup and walk, or go on the way to the airport.

turning-torso.name: Turning Torso
turning-torso.price_text: Free to see from outside · not open to the public inside
turning-torso.hours: Always visible · viewing from outside only
turning-torso.tip: See it from the Malmö waterfront or the beach at Ribersborg. You cannot go inside.

torvehallerne.name: Torvehallerne food market
torvehallerne.price_text: Free to enter · food about DKK 50–120 per item
torvehallerne.hours: Usually 10:00–19:00 weekdays, longer Saturday · check on the day
torvehallerne.tip: Two glass halls of stalls. Go hungry and try a Danish pastry, coffee and a smørrebrød.

rundetaarn-view.name: Christiansborg Tower viewpoint
rundetaarn-view.tip: Free lift to the top of the tower. Best on a clear day for views over the roofs and harbour.

harbour-bus.name: Harbour bus (Havnebussen)
harbour-bus.price_text: Normal city transport ticket, about DKK 24–36
harbour-bus.tip: A cheap boat ride through the harbour using a normal metro ticket. Sit outside at the back.

norrebro-walk.name: Nørrebro and Jægersborggade walk
norrebro-walk.tip: Walk Jægersborggade for small shops and coffee, then cross to Assistens Cemetery park for a quiet break.

vesterbro-meatpacking.name: Vesterbro and Kødbyen walk
vesterbro-meatpacking.hours: Streets always open · bars and restaurants from afternoon to late
vesterbro-meatpacking.tip: The old meatpacking district is now bars and galleries. Good for an evening walk and dinner.

kongens-have.name: King's Garden (Kongens Have)
kongens-have.hours: Usually 07:00–22:00 in summer · shorter in winter
kongens-have.tip: The city's oldest park. Bring a coffee and sit on the grass next to Rosenborg Castle.

stays.why: Walk to Nyhavn, Tivoli, the palaces and the Round Tower. Best for a first short visit.
Next to the central station and Tivoli; lively food and bar streets. Easy airport trains.
Cheaper, young and multicultural. Good cafés and street food; 10–15 min by bike or metro to the centre.
Quiet, leafy and close to the Little Mermaid, the lakes and the park. Good for families.

food: Start with smørrebrød: rye bread with herring, egg and shrimp. Lunch portions are bigger than they look.
Try a bakery 'kanelsnegl' (cinnamon roll) and Danish pastries; they are cheapest to take away.
Rejsekort or the app for cheap eats: hot dogs from a pølsevogn stand cost about DKK 30–45.
Nørrebro and Vesterbro have the best value: falafel, shawarma and street food halls, about DKK 60–100 a meal.
Book dinner ahead on weekends. A sit-down dinner with drinks often runs DKK 250–450 per person.
more_time: Swap a city day for Roskilde: the Viking Ship Museum and the cathedral, about 25 min by S-train.
Take the train to Louisiana Museum of Modern Art north of the city; check opening days on the day.
Cross to Malmö, Sweden, by train over the Øresund bridge for a half-day change of scene.
